slides.say: Which of the following numbers is prime?

So four numbers, all odd, and every one of them looks prime. But three of them are fakes, and only one is really prime. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, testing each number up to its root, and then counting by sevens.

[short pause] For each choice, we're looking for a divisor other than one and the number itself. Finding even one such divisor is enough to rule out a prime. Remember, to test a number, I divide it by the primes up to its square root, and no further. If none of them divides it, it's prime. Let's start with ninety-one. Nine squared is eighty-one, and ten squared is a hundred. So the root of ninety-one is between nine and ten, and I only try two, three, five and seven.

Two? Ninety-one is odd, so no. Three? Here's a quick test, and it's worth knowing well. Add the digits, and if the digit sum divides by three, the whole number does too. Fifty-one, five plus one is six, and six divides by three. And really, fifty-one is three times seventeen. But fifty-two, five plus two is seven, so fifty-two doesn't divide by three. We don't need to prove this test, it simply always works.

So ninety-one, nine plus one is ten. Ten doesn't divide by three, so three doesn't divide ninety-one. Five? It doesn't end in zero or five, so no. And seven? Seven has no quick test, so I just divide. Seven times ten is seventy, and seven times three is twenty-one, together ninety-one. So ninety-one is seven times thirteen. It breaks, it's a fake, and choice number one is out.

A hundred nineteen. Ten squared is a hundred, and eleven squared is a hundred twenty-one, so again I try two, three, five and seven. It's odd. One plus one plus nine is eleven, not a multiple of three. It ends in nine, so not five. And seven? Seven times ten is seventy, and seven times seven is forty-nine, together a hundred nineteen. So it's seven times seventeen, a fake again, and choice number two is out.

A hundred thirty-three. Eleven squared is a hundred twenty-one, and twelve squared is a hundred forty-four, so I try up to eleven. It's odd, one plus three plus three is seven, and it ends in three. Seven? Seven times twenty is a hundred forty, and one seven less is a hundred thirty-three. So it's seven times nineteen, and choice number four is out.

Three choices are already out. For this explanation, let's finish the prime test on the remaining number. In the exam you'd circle the last one and move on. Here, let's see why a hundred thirteen really is prime. Ten squared is a hundred and eleven squared is a hundred twenty-one, so I try two, three, five and seven. It's odd. One plus one plus three is five, not a multiple of three. It ends in three. And seven times sixteen, seventy plus forty-two, is a hundred twelve. So a hundred thirteen leaves a remainder of one.
Nothing up to the root divides it, so a hundred thirteen is prime. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: And look, all three fakes broke on seven. So when a number looks prime, never forget to try seven.

[pause] Our second method, counting by sevens. Why sevens? Because two, three and five have quick tests you can see on the number, even, the digit sum and the last digit. Seven is the one small prime with no quick test. So let's list the multiples of seven around a hundred.
at: two, three and five have quick tests

slides.say: We'll use the multiples of seven to check which answer choices contain a seven as a factor. Seven times thirteen is ninety-one. Then I add seven each time. Ninety-one plus seven is ninety-eight, plus seven is a hundred five, then a hundred twelve, a hundred nineteen, a hundred twenty-six, and a hundred thirty-three.
Ninety-one, a hundred nineteen and a hundred thirty-three are all on the list. So they divide by seven, they're fakes, and choice numbers one, two and four are out.
A hundred thirteen isn't on the list, and the other three choices are out. So there's nothing left to check, it's choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
